catalog_quote: 2.4 Tone • Two contrastive levels: H and L – Here, H is marked (e.g., [á]) and L is unmarked; both are marked in contours (e.g., [áà]) ... • Underlying tone melodies can be H, L, or LH. The same set of melodies is found on monomoraic and longer morphemes. • Interestingly, there are no monomoraic (CV) H-toned nouns (though there are H-toned CV morphemes in other categories). • Contour tones are only possible on heavy syllables (CVV, CVL). – For this reason, I assume the tone-bearing unit is a mora. • Most morphemes are specified underlyingly for tone. • Tone on a toneless affix (e.g., plural, imperfective) is determined by the stem (5). ... • Lobi displays downstep when a morpheme containing a H tone follows another morpheme containing a H tone in the same domain. sweep_summary: Lobi (lobi1245) is coded tonal on Sande 2025 (ACAL 56 handout, two-level H/L lexical tone, no stress/accent statement) backed by Becuwe 1982 as carried in Hoffmann. this search of works with stress in the title has a single item: Palé, Sami 1983 'Essai de représentation suprasegmentale des tons du lobiri', an unpublished Dakar FLSH mémoire known only from Maho's EBALL via Glottolog (ref 87696). By title and keywords it is a tone-representation study (prosody but not word stress); no open copy, holding, or citing text could be located (Glottolog record. Extra checks made in this search of works with stress in the title: Haumant 1929 'Les Lobi et leur coutume' (archive.org scanned, 0 accent/stress hits), Persée 'lobiri' hits (none phonological), HAL (0), LangSci CAL catalog on 2026-09-17 (Sande & Hien 'Aspects of Lobi grammar' still unpublished). No first-hand stress statement was read; the catalog's tonal coding and its Sande 2025 deciding source stand unchanged. Acquisition priorities remain, in order, the forthcoming Sande & Hien grammar and Becuwe 1982 (both already on the list of works to obtain), then Palé 1983 (medium).

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote verified verbatim in the Sande ACAL56 text we hold layer (sec. 2.4, pp.3-4) and the Becuwe carry in Hoffmann p.7; zero 'stress'/'accent' tokens in either Sande handout. The 'tonal' classification rests on 2025 primary fieldwork by a specialist phonologist corroborated by the 1982 thesis (second-hand) and Fané 2007 (via Wikipedia) — three independent descriptions agree on a two-level lexical tone system, so the kind is safe and no reclassification is indicated. What keeps this from 'well-sourced' is that the deciding document is a conference handout and the two full descriptions (Becuwe 1982, 480 pp; Sande & Hien 'Aspects of Lobi grammar', LangSci, accepted but unpublished as of 2026-09-16) are not yet obtained, so the absence of any stress/accent statement is silence of a handout rather than of a grammar; domain stays not stated by the source. Action: re-read when the LangSci grammar appears (open access) or if Becuwe
